name: Jindal Drilling
why: Working capital healthy - debtor days 90 to 82, inventory days n/a (not rising)
Promoters raised their stake by 2.4 pts in a year
Profits backed by cash: operating cash flow is 209% of 3-year profit
Sector cycle: Earnings improving but price not confirming
risks: Not at record: quarterly profit, annual profit
Margins shrinking (42% to 36%) - record profit may be near peak
Latest concall: management tone cautious (headwinds / delays mentioned)
Latest quarter Jun 2026: Weak (sales +8% YoY, profit -29% YoY)
FIIs (foreign funds) cut holding by 1.6 pts in a year
Cost quality weak: margin shrinking or operating profit falling (costs 58% to 64% of sales)

order_book: The order book stands at INR1,310 crores, and we've also bifurcated the order book year-wise.

The rate is something on which I cannot comment because if you look at our order book on Slide 5, you will see the massive fluctuation in the day rates despite these rigs getting redeployed in a similar time period.
guidance: That rig is currently under refurbishment in UAE, and we expect to deploy it as early as October of 2026.

And we've guided earlier that you should target a blended EBITDA of 3 5%, I think you will be able to make a fairly accurate assessment of the way the revenue will shape up in the second half of the current financial yea
risks: Despite that challenge, we remain fairly confident that we'll be able to redeploy these three rigs.
focus: So instead of having more assets which we have to deploy with ONGC, we are focusing on getting those assets deployed, which are going to get dehired in the later part of this financial year.
And my second question for you, sir, is for the three rigs that will be available for new contracts after refurbishment, are we looking at domestic or are we targeting international as well?
